title: Load balancing
subtitle: NAT pools in round-robin and source-hash, plus dup-to

segments.text: Load balancing in pf is done with pools. This rule translates the source of the client network into a pool of two addresses, the two gateways of the firewall, and selects between them round robin.
We capture on the interface towards the server to see which source address each packet carries.
And the capture shows the truth: three packets went out with one address, three with the other. The pool is really rotating between its members, and the server sees a balanced load.
Sometimes you do not want rotation. source hash keeps a given origin always mapped to the same pool member, which is what you want when a session has to be sticky.
Four more packets, and now every single one carries the same source address. The mapping is stable per origin.
segments.diagram_caption: every packet with the same source

segments.text: And dup to is the mirror case: the packet keeps its normal path, and a copy is delivered to the second gateway. We count the requests on both interfaces: one on the normal path, one on the mirrored path. The packet was duplicated, not moved.
segments.diagram_caption: dup-to: the normal path and the mirrored copy
